Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION NO. 20 s. 2024 FEB EDNA EARL H. IGNALAGUE Secretary to the Sanggunian Office of the Sangguniang Bayan Municipality of San Enrique Province of Negros Occidental Dear Ms. Ignalague: This refers to your electronic mail dated July 21, 2023 in relation to the letter dated June 29, 2023 of Carlo Raymund D. Magno, Municipal Vice-Mayor, Presiding Officer, Sangguniang Bayan, Municipality of San Enrique, Province of Negros Occidental seeking legal opinion as to the status of Resolution No. 2023-114 entitled "RESOLUTION DECLARING THE MUNICIPALITY OF SAN ENRIQUE, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL UNDER A STATE OF CALAMITY DUE TO HOG CHOLERA" dated 17 May 2023 adopted by the Sangguniang Bayan of the Municipality of San Enrique, Province of Negros Occidental, Per the letter of Vice-Mayor Magno, he explained that during the June 29, 2023 session of the Sangguniang Bayan, Hon. Roy A. Delos Santos inquired about the status of Resolution No. 2023-114 dated May 17, 2023 declaring the Municipality of San Enrique under a State of Calamity due to Hog Cholera. Hon. Delos Santos expressed that the Mayor has not acted upon said Resolution within the prescribed period as provided for in Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), hence the same is now effective. Under this premise arose the request for legal opinion regarding the status of the afore- stated resolution. Republic Act No. 10121 or the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2020 governs the national and local declaration of State Calamity. Section 16 of the said law provides: "Section 16. Declaration of State of Calamity. — The National Council shall recommend to the President of the Philippines the declaration of a cluster of barangays, municipalities, cities, provinces, and regions under a state of calamity, and the lifting thereof, based on the criteria set by the National Council. The President's declaration may warrant international humanitarian assistance as deemed necessary. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The declaration and lifting of the state of calamity may also be issued by the local san unian u on the recommendation of the LDRRMC based on the results of the dama e assessment and needs anal sis." This is reiterated under Section 2, Rule 12 (Declaration of State of Calamity) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 10121, thus: "RULE 12- DECLARATION OF STATE OF CALAMITY xxxx Section 2. Declaration and lifting of State of Calamity by the Local Sanggunian—The declaration and lifting Of the state of calamity may also be issued by the local sanggunian, upon recommendation of the LDRRMC, based on the results of the damage assessment and needs analysis. xxxx This is further reiterated under NDRRMC Memorandum Order No. 60, series of 2019 entitled "Revised Guidelines for the Declaration of a State of Calamity". "State of Calamity" as defined in Item 2(a) of said NDRRMC Memorandum Order refers to "a condition involving mass casualty and/or major damages to the environment, property, infrastructures, disruption of means of livelihoods and businesses, and normal way of life of people in the affected areas as a result of the occurrence of natural or human- induced hazard, which includes a calamity brought about by "hog cholera". Items 4 (a) and 6 of the NDRRMC Memorandum Order provide: "4. AUTHORITY TO DECLARE A STATE OF CALAMITY a. The Local Declaration. The declaration and lifting of the State of Calamity may be issued primarily by the local Sanggunian, upon the recommendation of the LDRRMC of the relevant LGU, adhering to the criteria set forth in this set of Guidelines. ii. iii. iv. The concerned LDRRMCs shall assess the situation using available tools [e.g. Rapid Damage Assessment and Needs Analysis (RDANA), Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA), and Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA)] to determine the satisfaction of criteria for the declaration of the State of Calamity as stipulated in Section 3. When two or more barangays are affected by a disaster, the Sangguniang Bayan or Panglunsod, upon the recommendation of the Municipal/City DRRM Council, may declare the entire municipality or city under a State of Calamity. When two or more municipalities or cities are affected by a the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, disaster, upon the recommendation of the Provincial DRRM Council, may declare the entire province under a State of Calamity. The concerned Sanggunian, through the LDRRMC, shall immediately fumish their respective Regional DRRM Council and the National DRRM Council a copy of the Sanggunian Resolution on the declaration of State of Calamity." Page 2 of 3

"6. DURATION AND LIFTING OF THE DECLARATION OF STATE OF CALAMITY The declaration of a State of Calamity may be enforced either by the President as recommended by the NDRRMC or the Local Chief Executive (LCE) upon the issuance of the corresponding Resolution by the local Sanggunian as recommended by the LDRRMC in the affected area for a duration of one (I) year or less, unless the effects of the disaster are recurring or protracted, in which case the declaration shall be a continuing one. However, the declaration of a State of Calamity shall be terminated or lifted by the local Sanggunian through a Resolution, or by the President through the recommendation of the NDRRMC, as the case may be." Based on the foregoing, the concerned local sanggunian, in this case, the sangguniang bayan, may declare a State of Local Calamity by adopting a Resolution for this purpose upon the recommendation of the LDRRMC. The participation of the LCE, in this case the Municipal, Mayor, is on the enforcement of the declaration of a State of Calamity. Accordingly, upon the adoption by the Sangguniang Bayan of its resolution declaring a state of calamity, the same may already be given effect by the Municipal Mayor. Let it be noted however that the aforequoted provisions of laws and rules governing the declaration of state of calamity require that the adoption of the resolution declaring a state of calamity by the concerned sanggunian must be upon recommendation of the LDRRMC. It appears that in Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 2023-114, such recommendation of the LDRRMC was not manifested. This should be revisited by the Sangguniang Bayan. This opinion is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRE R R. LLAMAS TTY. JUAN nde for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSE-LA/JRULL S-LRALLD/rjki/cIp copy furnished: DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E.
